svg.title: danielgarcia.it: how a page is rendered and how its language is chosen
svg.text: How a page is rendered, and how its language is chosen
Example: the French home page /. The English page /en/ follows exactly the same path with lang: en.
the page: front matter + its own content
No <!DOCTYPE at the start: a fragment,
so Roq wraps it in the "page" layout.
interface texts, one file per language
Roq Data turns the folder into one object:
the layout: written once, used by every page
the HTML sent to the browser for /
the engine that assembles the page
Roq reads the page, its front matter
and the layout; Qute replaces every
shortcuts for the front matter keys
Roq reads content/index.html: the front matter becomes page (title, description, data.lang, data.translation), the body goes to {#insert /}.
The layout reads page.data.lang (fr) and takes the matching file: t = the content of fr.yml, so t.role and t.languageSwitch are in French.
Qute replaces every {…} of the layout and inserts the body. The result is a complete HTML page, written to target/roq/index.html.
